answer: Seats are bound to geology, not keys. A seat must own one named bench on a specific mesa: each epoch its operator quarries a ferrous concretion, cuts it, and files the banding of its crystal-lined vug. Those bands record centuries of groundwater chemistry and lightning strikes, so they cannot be precomputed; the first cut destroys the vug. Neighbouring bench holders countersign sections, so a fake identity must fool two real neighbours. A sybil pays a permit, bench, saw and a day of labour, none shareable, and two seats on one bench yield identical bands, so both lose their bonds.
